A resolution introduces a big nef nonample class on the source; no equation theorem in that class is supplied.
Compactness, envelopes, first variation, full-mass operator, comparison, and rigidity on the singular space remain unproved.

exact_result: An isometric valued-field extension of a nondiscretely valued field cannot become discretely valued: its value group contains the original one. Thus discretization by scalar extension cannot supply the missing arbitrary-field operator.
gaps: No mixed finite-energy Monge--Ampere operator outside the established toric skeletal endpoint is constructed.
Approximation independence, mass tails, base-change descent, envelopes, and first variation over arbitrary complete fields are missing.
Existence and uniqueness in the residual scope are missing.
PS23 Remark 4.4 is available only through the catalogue and local secondary packet in this checkout.

exact_result: For K=C((t)), X=P^1 x P^1, and L=pr_1^*O(1), two nonconstant-separated continuous semipositive model metrics have the same zero genuine top-degree model Monge--Ampere measure. This rules out raw zero-volume top-degree MA with the entire continuous semipositive cone and uniqueness modulo constants; it is a diagnostic of a naive extension, not a solution of the atom permitting replacement conventions.
gaps: No equation theory for a general big nonample class is constructed.
The zero-volume diagnostic does not disprove the existence of every possible replacement positivity or mass convention.
No reference singularity type, corrected zero-volume theory, envelope differentiation, or comparison/rigidity replacement is supplied.
No new narrower equation theorem is claimed; no partial paper is presented.

exact_result: On the known smooth ample discretely valued P^1 case, nu_k=(1-1/k)delta_{x_0}+(1/k)delta_{x_{k^4}} is a genuine model MA measure, converges to delta_{x_0} in total variation norm 2/k, and has finite dual energy at least k^2/2. Weak or total-variation approximation alone gives no uniform dual-energy bound. This does not obstruct existence and does not address arbitrary support.
gaps: No arbitrary-support finite-energy existence theorem is established.
A measure approximation would need strong energy control and completion by actual pointwise potentials, not only weak measure convergence.
Attainment of the variational supremum and the integral semicontinuity needed for arbitrary measures are unproved.
The diagnostic remains entirely in the known model/skeletal range and is not counted as new equation progress.

gaps: An explicit positivity datum on a genuinely nonalgebraizable example is missing.
Global psh compactness, envelopes, energy and total mass, mixed products, and comparison/rigidity are missing.
